FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Metal Containers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1994. While reviewing this standard in light of experience gained during 
these years. The Committee felt to review this standard. While revising this standard international practices have 
been duly considered along with the specific Indian scenario. 


In this revision following modifications have been made: 


a) Dimensions of Drum A and Drum B have been modified. 

b) Construction clauses have been modified. 

c) Figure 1 and Figure 2 have been modified as per International Standard. 
d) Clause on locking has been modified. 


In the formulation of this standard assistance has been derived from ISO 15750-1- ‘Packaging — Steel drums — 
Part 1 Removable head (open head) drums with a minimum total capacity of 208 1, 210 1 and 216, 5 I’, issued by 
the International Organization for standardization. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. 


IS 13997 : 2014 


Indian Standard 
DRUMS, LARGE OPEN TOP — SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers the requirements for steel open 
top drums of 200 litre [180 kg] nominal capacity with 
bottom end fixed in the following types of construction: 


a) Grade A — Drums of steel sheets of nominal 
thickness 1.25 mm for body and end, with 
bottom seam of either double seam 
construction or spiral/triple seam construction 
and top full size openable drum lid. 


b) Grade B — Drums of steel sheets of nominal 
thickness 1.00 mm for body and end, with 
bottom end seam of spiral/triple seam 
construction and top full size openable lid. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contains provisions, which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of the publication, the editions 
indicated below were valid. All the standards are subject 
to revision, and parties to agreement based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
applying the most recent edition of the standard. 


IS No. Title 


513 : 2008 Cold reduced low carbon steel sheets 


and strips (fifth revision) 


1394 : 1984 Glossary of terms relating to metal 
containers (third revision) 

1784 : 1998 Screwed closures for drums (third 
revision) 

3259 : 1966 Methods of sampling of metal 
containers 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in IS 1394 shall apply. 


4 CAPACITY 


The minimum gross capacity of the drums measured 
with water at ambient temperature shall be 210 litre 
with lid fitted on the drums. 


5 DIMENSIONS 


The drums of Grade A and Grade B construction shall 


have dimensions as given in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 
respectively and as per Table 1. 


6 MATERIAL 


6.1 The body and ends of both Grade A and Grade B 
drums shall be made from cold reduced carbon steel 
sheets conforming to Grade CR1, CR2 or CR3 of 
IS 513. 


6.2 The nominal thickness of steel sheets for body 
and ends of the drums shall be 1.25 mm for Grade A 
and 1.00 mm for Grade B drums. 


6.3 The sheets and blanks may be phosphatized by 
any of the recognized processes, if required by the 
purchaser. 


7 CONSTRUCTION 


7.1 The sheets shall be blanked and formed to shape. 
The blanks shall be free from cracks, dents, pitting, 
rust and other defects. 


7.2 The body shall be continuously resistance welded 
so as to provide an airtight joint. 


7.3 Double Seam/Spiral Seam/Triple Seam 
Construction for Grade A Drums 


The bottom end shall be either double seamed or spiral/ 
triple seamed to the body using sealing compound 
resistant to the product to be packed as shown in Fig. 1. 


7.4 Spiral Seam/Triple Seam Construction for 
Grade B Drums 


The bottom end shall be seamed to the body as shown 
in Fig. 2. The seam shall have rolled 6 or more layers 
of sheet with the sealing compound forming a core at 
the joint of body and end sheet. The sealing compound 
forming the core shall be flexible and chemically 
resistant to the product to be packed. 


7.5 The top lid shall be recessed pressed suitably 
formed to fit the curled contour of the body and receive 
a sealing gasket of a suitable cross-section. 


7.6 The removable top end shall be fitted with a gasket 
of suitable material.

Fic. 1 DRUM WITH OPEN Top (GRADE A) 


7.7 Drums shall be provided with two rolling beads or 
hoops expanded or rolled in the drum body, located as 
shown in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2. Constructions of rolling 
hoops other than those shown are allowed. 


7.8 Grade B drums shall be provided with 
strengthening corrugations on the body having at least 
4 mm depth measured from crest to trough. Four 
numbers on each side located symmetrically between 
the end seams and the rolling hoops as shown in Fig. 2. 
Constructions of corrugations other than those shown 
are allowed. 


7.9 Closures 


The top lid of the drum shall normally be without any 
closures, but if required by the purchaser, a suitable 
closure shall be provided as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. 


7.10 If additional closures are provided in the top end, 
the following applies: 


a) Closures shall be positioned in the top end, 
diametrical opposed as indicated in Fig. 1; 
b) Closures should be as specified in IS 1784; 


c) Gaskets/washers or other sealing elements 
shall be used with the closures unless the 
fittings are inherently leak proof; and 


d) Metal or plastics plugs shall be fitted with 
washers/gaskets of suitable material. 


7.11 Locking Ring 


The construction of the locking ring shall be such that 
the tightness of the drum is not jeopardized. 


8 FINISH 


8.1 The drum shall be in clean condition, the inside

being free from all traces of dust and foreign matter. 


8.2 If the materials used for the body, heads and fittings 
are not in themselves compatible with contents to be 
transported, suitable internal protective coatings or 
treatments shall be applied. These coatings or 
treatments shall retain their protective properties under 
normal conditions of transport. 


9 TESTS 


9.1 The side and the bottom joints shall be water-tight. 
If agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, 
the open top drums may be checked for leakage when 
filled with water. For doing the test, the drum shall be 
filled with water up to the brim and kept for | h. There 
shall be no leakage either through the body or through 
the side and bottom seam joint. 


9.2 If there is a minor leakage found during leakage 
test, it may be manually welded and the drum shall be 
retested for leakage. If the leakage is found again, the 
drum shall be rejected. 


10 SAMPLING 


Representative sample of the drums for tests regarding 


dimensions, capacity, construction, finish, leakage, 
shall be drawn as prescribed in IS 3259. 


11 MARKING 


11.1 Each drum shall be marked legibly and indelibly 
with the following particulars by embossing with raised 
markings or screen printing on the bottom: 


a) Indication of the source of the manufacturer; 
b) Grade and type of the drum; and 


c) Any other information as required by the 
purchaser. 


11.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The drums may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


11.2.1 The use of Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of Bureau of Indian Standard Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder 
govern the use of the Standard Mark. The details of 
conditions under which the license for the use of 
Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian 
Standards. 


Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MTD 32 (5097).
